title: Feature Catalog by Origin
heading: Inspect a sales discrepancy
text:
Inspect a sales discrepancy
Open the source's sales page. Check its definition of a sale and the fixed rules visible in the SQL: the two ERPs do not measure the same relation.
Choose the measure and grouping to open the complete SQL. Copy or download it in the portal, then bind the documented example parameters in your database client. Examples contain synthetic dates/phrases, no ERP records or credentials.
Match the actual date interval, literal or semantic product selection and effective permission restrictions. A restriction by sale-time buyer differs from filtering the current product registration buyer. Quantity partitions must retain their unit/packaging.
For comparisons, use the separate comparison bindings. previous_period is an equal-day interval, not necessarily the preceding calendar month. Both periods use the same current product membership.
Documentation reading never queries an ERP. Downloaded SQL runs only when you explicitly execute it through your own authorized database client. The examples document the production compiler; they are not captured SQL from a particular person's request or proof of live ERP reconciliation.

title: Feature Catalog by Origin
heading: Maintenance
text:
Maintenance
The [composition](../../apps/api/src/modules.ts) owns which runtime modules and capabilities exist. This index routes to their canonical domain documentation. When adding/removing a product function, update its row here in the same change; do not maintain a second normative description in this index. The [OpenAPI reference](../generated/api/openapi.json) contains the exhaustive HTTP operation inventory, including administrative and operational endpoints.
SQL variants, supported measures/groupings, filter dimensions, exposure status and access predicates are generated from the production compilers/catalogs by [feature-reference.ts](../../apps/api/scripts/feature-reference.ts). Run `pnpm -C apps/api references:write`, then `pnpm docs:references:write`. The corresponding check commands reject drift. No environment file, model call or ERP connection is needed to generate these feature references; the broader API reference command also verifies the migrated local application schema as usual.

title: Web Component Reference
heading: States
text:
States

Compact add menu
Floating attachment or preference view
Empty
Owned attachments
Selected file awaiting purpose and explicit approval
Client file-format or size feedback
Saving
Saved confirmation
Validation or access failure
Accessibility: The labeled plus trigger exposes an expanded state and opens a named modeless native popover. Keyboard focus enters its options, Escape and outside clicks dismiss it, and explicit close restores trigger focus. Named sections, shared labeled controls, an explicit approval checkbox and live status/alert messages retain the material workflow.
Usage: Place the trigger inside the message composer. Its compact menu opens a file picker, existing attachment metadata or presentation settings. A viewport-bounded floating panel follows the composer without displacing the conversation; its portal sits outside the message form to prevent accidental submission from material fields. File selection remains local until explicit upload; replacing the file clears approval. Bounds, discard, retry IDs and dependent-reply removal remain intact. The server remains authoritative for ownership, limits and restricted-data policy.

[Configuration policy](../../architecture/configuration.md) · [API runtime](../../../apps/api/README.md)
No values are eligible for client exposure. `ORION_ENV` is always required. The three token settings are configured together. API modules that require the database or bearer authentication stay unmounted until those settings exist, and production startup fails instead.
Role says why a setting is an environment variable: `bootstrap` (infrastructure, deployment or trust configuration; changed by deployment and restart), `secret` (credential or key; never exposed through an API or interface), `parameter` (installation default of an [operational parameter](../../architecture/configuration.md#operational-parameters) that owners override at run time) or `development` (local development and testing only).

text:
agent_conversations
Actor-owned corporate agent conversation with capability-specific validated context and a bounded execution lease.
Owner: agent. Classification: CONFIDENTIAL.
Lifecycle: Local history persists until the owner explicitly deletes the conversation. Conversation deletion cascades to turns and contexts. No automatic expiry is implemented; shared deployment requires an owner-defined retention/backups/provider policy before rollout. No vector, export or replica copies are created by the application.

title: Database Reference
heading: agent_turn_traces
text:
agent_turn_traces
Optional content-level AI trace of one turn, written only when IA_MNS_AI_TRACE=content: model/prompt identifiers, timings and token counts, routing and interpretation decisions, structured conversation state before and after, and the executed query filters. Never result rows, response prose, credentials or provider payloads. Used to reproduce failures and derive evaluation candidates.
Owner: agent. Classification: CONFIDENTIAL.
Lifecycle: Written in the same transaction as the turn outcome and deleted by cascade with its turn or conversation. The runtime role can only append and read. Content capture is refused in production until the shared-deployment retention and access policy (PH-09) approves it. No automatic expiry is implemented.

whatsapp_inbound_messages
WhatsApp messages from senders that matched exactly one active Person through an owner-linked number when the signature-verified webhook arrived. Unknown, unlinked or unauthorized senders are never recorded. Each row is processed once, in order per Person, after the sender is authorized again.

whatsapp_outbound_messages
Replies to inbound WhatsApp messages: an outbox of text parts sent through the Graph API only after the recipient is authorized again for the same Person and link version, and only within the customer service window.
Owner: whatsapp. Classification: CONFIDENTIAL.
Lifecycle: Created when processing produces a reply; sent in part order under a lease; retried only when Meta proves the message was not accepted (rate limits, temporary unavailability); a timeout or lost response becomes unknown and is never resent. Delivery statuses from signed webhooks advance the state. The text is cleared once Meta accepts the part or it reaches a final state. Pruned with its inbound message.
